BiblicalUsage: Zelah was a town in Benjamin, named in the allotment of the tribe and as the burial place of Saul and Jonathan. After the famine, David gathered the bones of Saul and Jonathan and buried them in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father. A town on a list became the resting place of Israel's first king.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the burial of Saul at Zelah closes a long story with honour — David gave his enemy a grave, and the land kept the memory. Even a king who fell is buried with dignity.
